bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42513013 (file): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target magic_fuzzer [asan].
bug_description.normalized: For the exact two-byte witness `20 74` (`" t"`), `file_buffer` calls `buffer_init(&b, fd, st, buf, nb)`, which stores the attacker-controlled pointer in `b->fbuf` and the length `2` in `b->flen`. `file_is_json` then derives `uc` and `ue` from those fields, and top-level `json_parse` skips the leading space so only the trailing `t` remains. The switch on `*uc++` dispatches that byte to `json_parse_const(&uc, ue, "true", sizeof("true"), ...)`, leaving `uc == ue` before the helper starts. In the vulnerable helper, `*ucp += --len - 1` advances the caller cursor by the remaining literal length without clamping it to `ue`, so with no bytes left after the initial `t` it writes `ue + 3` back into the caller's `uc`. Because the comparison loop is guarded by `uc < ue`, the missing `rue` suffix is never checked and the truncated constant is accepted as successful. Back in top-level `json_parse`, the exact-end guard checks only `uc == ue`, misses the overshoot state `uc > ue`, and the newline-delimited JSON retry `if (*ouc == *uc && json_parse(...))` dereferences the out-of-bounds cursor. AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at `src/is_json.c:407`.

source.description: First project-side statement on the crashing path that consumes the fuzzer-supplied buffer and length by materializing them into `struct buffer b`.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is the exact 2-byte blob `20 74` (hex), i.e. ASCII `" t"`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` passes those bytes to `magic_buffer`, which forwards them as `buf` and `nb` into `file_buffer`; this call hands them to `buffer_init`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The top-level newline-delimited-JSON retry dereferences `*uc` after `json_parse_const` has advanced `uc` past `ue`.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `READ of size 1` at `src/is_json.c:407`, with faulting address `0x602000000115`, which is 3 bytes to the right of the 2-byte input region `[0x602000000110,0x602000000112)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `json_parse_const` advances the caller's cursor by the remaining keyword length without checking that the new pointer stays within the `[start, ue]` input range.
root_cause.note: When called for `"true"`, `sizeof("true")` is 5, so this line decrements `len` to 4 and then adds 3 to the caller cursor. For the witness, the caller cursor already equals `ue`, so `*ucp` becomes `ue + 3`. The fix adds `if (*ucp > ue) *ucp = ue;` immediately after this line.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call is where the tainted pointer/length pair first becomes persistent parser state; the next two trace steps are the concrete `buffer_init` field writes to `b->fbuf` and `b->flen`.

parser_admitted.description: After earlier compression and tar checks, `file_buffer` reaches the JSON classifier on the attacker-controlled `struct buffer b`. The saved ASan stack confirms the crashing path `file_buffer -> file_is_json -> json_parse`.

coarse_trace.summary: The libFuzzer harness passes the exact 2-byte witness `20 74` into `magic_buffer`.

The project first consumes the attacker buffer in `file_buffer`, which calls `buffer_init` to store the raw pointer in `b->fbuf` and the length in `b->flen`; later in the same function it reaches `file_is_json` on that state.
The JSON parser derives `uc` and `ue` from `b->fbuf` and `b->flen`, skips the leading space, and dispatches the lone trailing `t` to `json_parse_const` as the start of `true`.

The constant parser advances the caller cursor past `ue` and returns success without checking the missing `rue` suffix; top-level `json_parse` then misses the `uc > ue` state and dereferences `*uc` in the newline-delimited JSON retry.

fine_trace.note: Source. `file_buffer` is the first project-side consumer of the fuzzer buffer on this path: it passes the raw `buf` pointer and `nb` length from `magic_buffer` into `buffer_init` so they become persistent `struct buffer b` state.
The input byte pointer is stored in `b->fbuf`, so later JSON parsing aliases the same 2-byte witness allocation rather than a copied buffer.
The input length is stored as `b->flen`. For the staged witness this value is `2`, which becomes the exclusive bound later used to form `ue`.

fine_trace.code: const unsigned char *uc = CAST(const unsigned char *, b->fbuf);
fine_trace.note: `file_is_json` aliases the stored buffer pointer as its parser cursor `uc`.
Derives the exclusive end pointer from the stored length. With `b->flen == 2`, the valid input range is `[uc, ue)` covering the two witness bytes `0x20 0x74`.
Top-level JSON parsing skips the leading space, so both `uc` and `ouc` now point at the lone in-bounds `t` byte at offset 1 while `ue` still points just past it.

fine_trace.code: switch (*uc++) { case 't': rv = json_parse_const(&uc, ue, "true", sizeof("true"), lvl + 1);
fine_trace.note: The switch reads that `t` via `*uc++`, selects the `true` constant arm, and increments the local cursor to `ue` before `json_parse_const` starts.

Root cause. `json_parse_const` blindly advances the caller-owned cursor by the remaining keyword length. For `sizeof("true") == 5`, `--len - 1` is 3, so `uc == ue` becomes `uc == ue + 3` with no clamp to `ue`.

fine_trace.code: for (; uc < ue && --len;) { if (*uc++ != *++str) { DPRINTF("Bad const: ", uc, *ucp); return 0; } }
fine_trace.note: The helper's local snapshot `uc` was taken before step 8 and is already equal to `ue`, so `uc < ue` is false and the loop never compares any of the missing `rue` bytes. The function returns success while the caller cursor stays overshot.

Because step 9 returned success, the `if (!rv) return 0;` check at line 403 does not fire. This exact-end guard checks only `uc == ue`, so it misses the overshoot state `uc > ue` and falls through to the retry logic.
ASan sink. `ouc` still points at the in-bounds `t` from step 6, but `uc` still equals `ue + 3`. Evaluating `*uc` in the retry predicate performs the reported 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_summary: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in json_parse; stack json_parse -> file_is_json -> file_buffer -> magic_buffer -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42513013 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `json_parse` with stack `json_parse -> file_is_json -> file_buffer -> magic_buffer -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: Exact 2-byte magic_fuzzer witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 2-byte file `poc`: hex `20 74`, i.e. ASCII `" t"`. On the saved run, `file_buffer` stores that pointer/length pair in `b->fbuf` and `b->flen`, `file_is_json` skips the leading space, and top-level `json_parse` dispatches the lone trailing `t` to `json_parse_const(..., "true", sizeof("true"))`. Because no `rue` bytes remain, the vulnerable helper advances the caller cursor 3 bytes past `ue`, returns success without comparing any suffix bytes, and the top-level retry `if (*ouc == *uc && json_parse(...))` dereferences that overshot cursor at line 407. The staged evidence does not establish a broader trigger contract beyond this exact 2-byte witness.
